title: Red Rising
notes: Felt juvenile -- reads like a high-school drama with teenagers fighting, spoiled bullies vs. an infiltrated poor kid. Felt unoriginal -- most concepts already seen in Hunger Games/Battle Royale. Felt preachy -- constantly pushes the message that revenge leads nowhere and that once you know your enemies they are not so different from you, which feels like a farfetched conclusion for a protagonist who lost everyone he loves and whose sole purpose is revenge.

title: The Poppy War
notes: Constant authorial push to make punishing the aggressor feel wrong -- a threat of annihilation is answered with annihilation of the other side, which the author frames as wrong; this rubbed the reader the wrong way. Compounded by being school-of-magic trope fatigued at the time of reading, independent of the book itself.
